questions.prompt: Which of the following best defines a project?
choices: An ongoing activity that has no defined ending.
A unique endeavor that usually includes a set of unique deliverables.
A repeated process designed to maintain daily operations.
A collection of unrelated tasks performed by an organization.
questions.explanation: A project is a unique endeavor with unique deliverables and a defined beginning and end.

questions.prompt: Which characteristic makes a project different from regular organizational operations?
choices: It requires employees to work together.
It always requires a large budget.
It is a temporary pursuit with a defined beginning and end.
questions.explanation: A project is temporary, while regular operations are generally ongoing.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of project management?
choices: To increase the number of employees working on a project.
To eliminate all risks associated with a project.
To apply knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to meet project requirements and achieve the desired outcome.
To ensure that every project finishes without any changes.
questions.explanation: Project management uses knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to meet project requirements.

questions.prompt: According to the slides, what percentage of projects miss their delivery dates because of poor project management?
questions.explanation: According to the PMI statistics shown in the slides, 48% of projects miss delivery dates.

questions.prompt: According to the slides, what percentage of projects miss their budget targets?
questions.explanation: 43% of projects miss their budget targets.

questions.prompt: According to the slides, what percentage of projects fail to meet an organization's goals?
questions.explanation: 31% of projects fail to meet organizational goals.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT listed as a task of a project manager?
choices: Guaranteeing that no project risks will occur.
questions.explanation: Project managers plan, organize, manage tasks, budget, and control project costs and other factors. They cannot guarantee that risks will never occur.

questions.prompt: A company appoints someone to organize tasks, manage the budget, and control project costs. What is this person's role?
questions.explanation: These responsibilities belong to the project manager.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes a stakeholder?
choices: Only an individual who directly works on project tasks.
Only an organization that provides financial resources.
Any individual, group, or organization that can affect, be affected by, or perceive themselves to be affected by a project.
Only the person responsible for approving the project.
questions.explanation: Stakeholders can have direct or indirect interests in a project's outcomes.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of a project stakeholder?
choices: A supplier providing materials or services.
Only employees who develop the final product.
questions.explanation: Suppliers are stakeholders because they provide materials or services required by the project.

questions.prompt: A company provides the budget and resources needed to develop a new application. Which stakeholder role does this describe?
questions.explanation: A project sponsor provides the budget and resources for the project.

questions.prompt: A government organization checks whether a new IT system follows legal requirements. What type of stakeholder is it?
questions.explanation: A regulatory body ensures that the project complies with legal requirements.

questions.prompt: Which statement about stakeholders is correct?
choices: All stakeholders have the same influence and power.
Stakeholders must always participate directly in project activities.
Stakeholders only become involved after project completion.
Their involvement can vary in influence, power, expectations, and roles.
questions.explanation: Stakeholders have different levels of influence, power, expectations, and involvement.

questions.prompt: Which principle focuses on acting responsibly with integrity, care, and trustworthiness?
questions.explanation: Stewardship involves responsible actions, integrity, care, trustworthiness, and compliance with guidelines.

questions.prompt: A project manager considers the financial, social, and environmental impacts of a project. Which principle is being applied?
questions.explanation: Stewardship includes a broad commitment to financial, social, and environmental impacts.

questions.prompt: A software development team combines different skills, knowledge, and experience to achieve one shared objective. Which principle does this demonstrate?
questions.explanation: The Team principle emphasizes collaboration and using diverse skills to accomplish shared objectives.

questions.prompt: According to the Team principle, why can collaborative teams be more effective than individuals working alone?
choices: They eliminate the need for project management.
They can accomplish shared objectives more effectively and efficiently.
They ensure that every team member has identical skills.
They remove the need for stakeholders.
questions.explanation: Collaboration allows individuals with different skills and knowledge to work toward a common objective.

questions.prompt: A project manager regularly communicates with customers and involves them when necessary to improve project success. Which principle is demonstrated?
questions.explanation: The Stakeholders principle focuses on proactive engagement to support project success and customer satisfaction.

questions.prompt: Which principle requires continually evaluating whether a project remains aligned with business objectives and intended benefits?
questions.explanation: The Value principle focuses on maintaining alignment with business objectives, benefits, and value.

questions.prompt: A company realizes that a project is no longer delivering the expected business benefits. The manager evaluates and adjusts the project's direction. Which principle is most relevant?
questions.explanation: Value requires continually evaluating and adjusting project alignment with business objectives and intended benefits.

questions.prompt: Which principle focuses on understanding the project and its surrounding circumstances as a whole?
questions.explanation: Systems Thinking involves recognizing, evaluating, and responding to circumstances within and surrounding the project in a holistic way.

questions.prompt: A project manager studies how changes in one department could affect other departments and the overall project. Which principle is demonstrated?
questions.explanation: Systems Thinking considers relationships and interactions across the entire project rather than examining individual parts separately.

questions.prompt: A manager changes their leadership behavior depending on the needs of individual team members. Which principle does this represent?
questions.explanation: Leadership requires demonstrating and adapting leadership behaviors to support individual and team needs.

questions.prompt: A project manager decides to use fewer processes for a small project instead of following unnecessary procedures. Which principle is being applied?
questions.explanation: Tailoring means designing the project development approach based on the project context and using just enough process to achieve the desired outcome.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is considered when tailoring a project development approach?
choices: Only the project's budget and schedule.
Only the project manager's personal preferences.
The project's context, objectives, stakeholders, governance, and environment.
Only the number of team members.
questions.explanation: Tailoring considers all these factors to maximize value, manage cost, and enhance speed.

questions.prompt: Which principle focuses on producing deliverables that meet project objectives and stakeholder requirements?
questions.explanation: Quality ensures deliverables meet project objectives and the needs, uses, and acceptance requirements of stakeholders.

questions.prompt: A software application works correctly but does not meet the customer's acceptance requirements. Which principle has not been properly achieved?
questions.explanation: Quality is not only about whether a product works; it must also meet stakeholder needs and acceptance requirements.

questions.prompt: Which principle involves continually evaluating and navigating project complexity throughout the project life cycle?
questions.explanation: Complexity focuses on evaluating project complexity and adjusting approaches and plans to navigate the project life cycle successfully.

questions.prompt: A project manager identifies possible opportunities and threats and evaluates their potential impact on the project. Which principle is being applied?
questions.explanation: Risk involves evaluating both opportunities and threats to maximize positive impacts and minimize negative impacts.

questions.prompt: What is the main objective of the Risk principle?
choices: Eliminate every possible threat before project execution.
Focus only on negative events that could affect the project.
Maximize positive impacts and minimize negative impacts on the project and its outcomes.
Transfer all project responsibilities to stakeholders.
questions.explanation: Risk considers both opportunities (positive impacts) and threats (negative impacts).

questions.prompt: A project experiences unexpected problems, but the team adjusts its approach and continues working toward the objectives. Which principle is demonstrated?
questions.explanation: Adaptability and Resilience help projects accommodate change, recover from setbacks, and advance project work.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains the difference between Adaptability and Resilience?
choices: Adaptability helps accommodate change, while resilience helps recover from setbacks.
Adaptability focuses on quality, while resilience focuses on cost.
Adaptability manages stakeholders, while resilience manages resources.
Adaptability prevents changes, while resilience eliminates risks.
questions.explanation: Both support the project team, but adaptability focuses on adjusting to change and resilience focuses on recovering from setbacks.

questions.prompt: A company introduces a new system and prepares employees to adopt different working behaviors and processes. Which principle is being applied?
questions.explanation: Change prepares those impacted to adopt and sustain new behaviors and processes during the transition to the intended future state.

questions.prompt: Which of the following correctly describes the Change principle?
choices: Preventing employees from changing their existing working methods.
Preparing those impacted for the adoption and sustainment of new and different behaviors and processes.
Changing the project budget whenever stakeholders request it.
Allowing project teams to ignore organizational processes.
questions.explanation: The Change principle focuses on preparing people for the transition from the current state to the intended future state.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT one of the 12 Principles of Project Management?
questions.explanation: Resource allocation is not listed as one of the 12 principles.

questions.prompt: Which of the following correctly identifies the five stages of the IT Project Management Lifecycle?
choices: Initiation, Planning, Execution, Monitoring and Controlling, Closing.
Initiation, Budgeting, Execution, Risk Management, Closing.
questions.explanation: These are the five stages shown in slide 21.

questions.prompt: What is the first stage of the IT Project Management Lifecycle?
questions.explanation: Project Initiation is the first stage of the lifecycle.

questions.prompt: Which stage focuses on creating a detailed roadmap that guides the project from start to completion?
questions.explanation: Project Planning creates a detailed roadmap to guide the project.

questions.prompt: During which stage does the project management team focus on completing the work defined in the project management plan?
questions.explanation: Project Execution translates the project management plan into action.

questions.prompt: A project manager tracks project progress, reviews performance, and takes action when problems arise. Which stage does this describe?
questions.explanation: Monitoring and Controlling focuses on tracking, reviewing, and regulating project progress and performance.

questions.prompt: Which stage ensures that all project work is finalized and deliverables are accepted?
questions.explanation: Project Closing formally completes the project and ensures that deliverables and administrative tasks are finalized.

questions.prompt: A company has an idea for developing a new mobile application. Before starting, it defines the project at a high level and checks whether it aligns with organizational goals. Which stage is this?
questions.explanation: Project Initiation establishes the groundwork, defines the project at a high level, and checks alignment with strategic goals.

questions.prompt: A project manager needs official authorization to begin a project and authority to use organizational resources. Which document should be developed?
questions.explanation: The Project Charter formally authorizes the project's existence and gives the project manager authority to apply organizational resources.

questions.prompt: A project manager records stakeholders' roles, expectations, and influence levels. Which document is being created?
questions.explanation: The Stakeholder Register documents stakeholder details, including their roles, expectations, and influence levels.

questions.prompt: Before approving a project, management analyzes its resources, budget, time, and potential constraints to determine whether it is viable. What activity is being performed?
questions.explanation: A feasibility study analyzes whether the project is viable based on resources, budget, time, and constraints.

questions.prompt: A project manager defines the project's purpose, key deliverables, boundaries, and success criteria at a high level. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: Defining High-Level Scope establishes the project's purpose, deliverables, boundaries, and success criteria.

questions.prompt: A project cannot proceed because senior management has not approved the required funding and resources. Which initiation activity is incomplete?
questions.explanation: Approval and Funding involves obtaining the necessary approval and securing funding and resources.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the main purpose of Project Initiation?
choices: To complete all project deliverables and obtain final acceptance.
To provide clarity on whether the project is worth pursuing and officially establish its foundation.
To monitor the project's actual spending against the budget.
To execute all tasks defined in the project management plan.
questions.explanation: Initiation determines whether a project is worth pursuing and establishes the foundation for planning and execution.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the Monitoring and Controlling stage is correct?
choices: It only begins after project execution has been completed.
It replaces the project management plan when problems occur.
It runs concurrently with Project Execution to track progress and ensure the project stays on track.
It focuses only on obtaining project approval.
questions.explanation: Monitoring and Controlling runs alongside execution and helps ensure that the project meets its objectives.

questions.prompt: A project manager identifies that a project is not meeting its expected performance. The manager reviews progress and regulates the work to address the problem. What is the main purpose of this activity?
choices: To establish the project's initial authorization.
To ensure that the project stays on track to meet its objectives.
To define the project's high-level scope.
questions.explanation: Monitoring and Controlling identifies performance problems and helps take corrective action to keep the project aligned with its objectives.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the Waterfall methodology?
choices: Completing all project phases at the same time
Completing project phases in a fixed sequence
Allowing requirements to change every day
questions.explanation: Waterfall follows a sequential process where one phase is completed before the next phase begins.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct order of the five Waterfall stages?
choices: Design â†’ Requirements â†’ Testing â†’ Implementation â†’ Operation
Requirements â†’ Implementation â†’ Design â†’ Testing â†’ Operation
Requirements â†’ Design â†’ Implementation â†’ Testing â†’ Operation
Design â†’ Implementation â†’ Requirements â†’ Operation â†’ Testing
questions.explanation: The five stages must be completed in this order.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the Requirements stage?
choices: To identify and document what the project needs
questions.explanation: The project manager gathers comprehensive information and prepares a requirements document.

questions.prompt: Which activity can be used to gather requirements?
questions.explanation: Requirements can be collected through interviews, questionnaires, and brainstorming.

questions.prompt: A project manager uses questionnaires to discover what users need. Which phase is this?
questions.explanation: Questionnaires are one method used to collect project requirements.

questions.prompt: What should be ready at the end of the Requirements stage?
questions.explanation: The requirements should be clear and documented for the project team.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the Design stage?
choices: To determine how the requirements will be satisfied
questions.explanation: The team designs solutions and specifications that satisfy the project's requirements.

questions.prompt: Which activity belongs to the Design stage?
questions.explanation: The team creates schedules, milestones, deliverables, designs, and blueprints during Design.

questions.prompt: What are project deliverables?
choices: Outputs that the project is expected to produce
questions.explanation: The Design stage includes determining the project's deliverables.

questions.prompt: A team creates blueprints for a new application. Which phase are they in?
questions.explanation: Creating designs and blueprints is part of the Design stage.

questions.prompt: When does Implementation begin?
questions.explanation: Implementation begins once the design has been finalized.

questions.prompt: What happens during Implementation?
questions.explanation: Implementation involves building the product according to the approved design and specifications.

questions.prompt: Which activity is part of Implementation?
questions.explanation: The project manager creates an implementation plan and assigns tasks and resources.

questions.prompt: Why are resources allocated during Implementation?
choices: To assign the necessary resources to project tasks
questions.explanation: The project manager assigns tasks and allocates resources among the team.

questions.prompt: A project manager assigns different programming tasks to team members. Which phase is this?
questions.explanation: Assigning tasks and allocating resources are Implementation activities.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Testing?
choices: To check the quality and functionality of the developed product
questions.explanation: Testing is the quality-assurance stage after the product has been developed.

questions.prompt: What does quality assurance do during Testing?
questions.explanation: Writing test cases is specifically listed as a Testing activity.

questions.prompt: What should happen to bugs found during Testing?
choices: They should be hidden from the team
questions.explanation: The Testing stage includes documenting bugs and errors that need to be fixed.

questions.prompt: Why does Waterfall testing cover different use-case scenarios?
choices: To ensure the product works in different situations
questions.explanation: Testing covers a variety of use cases and environments to help ensure a good user experience.

questions.prompt: Which phase comes immediately after Implementation?
questions.explanation: After the product is developed during Implementation, it goes through Testing.

questions.prompt: What happens during Operation?
choices: The completed product is delivered to the client
The team creates the first prototype
questions.explanation: Operation involves releasing the completed product to the client.

questions.prompt: After release, who informs the team about issues that arise?
questions.explanation: After release, the client informs the team about issues that arise.

questions.prompt: What can the team create to fix problems after release?
questions.explanation: During Operation, bugs may be addressed through patches and newer product versions.

questions.prompt: Which is a major characteristic of Waterfall?
questions.explanation: Waterfall requires each phase to be completed before the next begins.

questions.prompt: What happens if a problem has not been resolved in a phase?
choices: The team must resolve it before moving forward
questions.explanation: The team cannot move to the next phase until problems in the current phase are resolved.

questions.prompt: Why is Waterfall considered structured?
choices: It has clearly defined sequential stages
questions.explanation: Waterfall follows a defined sequence from Requirements through Operation.

questions.prompt: Which benefit comes from rigorous planning?
questions.explanation: Rigorous planning creates a clear goal and reduces confusion.

questions.prompt: Why can Waterfall have a predictable cost and schedule?
choices: Because planning is done thoroughly before implementation
questions.explanation: Detailed planning allows the team to know the expected cost and schedule before implementation.

questions.prompt: Why is progress easier to track in Waterfall?
choices: Different phases are not being worked on in parallel
questions.explanation: The sequential structure makes it easier to identify the project's current stage and progress.

questions.prompt: What does a replicable process mean?
choices: The same successful process can be used for similar projects
The project must restart every day
questions.explanation: A successful Waterfall process can be reused for projects with similar requirements.

questions.prompt: How does Waterfall help with risk management?
choices: Through thorough planning at the beginning
questions.explanation: Early planning can help identify issues before implementation begins.     Waterfall Project Management MeÂ²

questions.prompt: Why can junior team members contribute more easily in Waterfall?
choices: The process and tasks are clearly defined
questions.explanation: The structured process can make it easier for less-experienced team members to participate.

questions.prompt: Why are additional requirements less likely to delay implementation?
questions.explanation: Once implementation starts, stakeholders cannot make additional requests under the Waterfall process described in the PDF.

questions.prompt: Which type of project is most suitable for Waterfall?
choices: A project where requirements change every day
A project with no defined goal
questions.explanation: Waterfall works well when requirements are known and stable.

questions.prompt: Why can Waterfall have longer delivery times?
questions.explanation: The sequential process can make final delivery take longer.

questions.prompt: What can happen when an unexpected event occurs?
choices: The project can experience a significant setback
questions.explanation: Unexpected events can significantly affect project time and cost.

questions.prompt: What is one reason Waterfall is vulnerable to setbacks?
choices: Each phase depends on successful completion of previous work
questions.explanation: A problem in one phase can prevent later phases from progressing normally.

questions.prompt: What is a limitation concerning client input?
choices: Client feedback is limited after requirements are gathered
questions.explanation: Once execution begins, stakeholders cannot normally add new requirements or provide ongoing feedback.

questions.prompt: Why might feature requests increase after launch?
choices: The client may only discover desired changes after seeing the finished product
questions.explanation: Limited client input during implementation can lead to additional requests after the product is delivered.

questions.prompt: What is deadline creep in Waterfall?
choices: Delays caused by problems in earlier phases affecting later phases
Finishing the project earlier than planned
questions.explanation: A problem in one phase can stop progress and push the entire schedule behind.

questions.prompt: A team discovers a major design problem before Implementation begins. What should they do?
choices: Resolve the problem before moving forward
questions.explanation: Waterfall requires problems in the current phase to be addressed before proceeding.

questions.prompt: A company knows exactly what product it wants and expects few requirement changes. Which methodology characteristic makes Waterfall appropriate?
questions.explanation: Waterfall is most suitable when requirements are predictable and stable.

questions.prompt: Which phase determines the project's schedules and milestones?
questions.explanation: Creating schedules and project milestones is listed as a Design activity.

questions.prompt: Which phase involves collecting data or conducting research needed to build the product?
questions.explanation: Implementation can include collecting data or conducting research needed for implementation.

questions.prompt: Which phase determines quality-assurance metrics?
questions.explanation: Determining which quality-assurance metrics to track is part of Testing.

questions.prompt: A completed product is handed to the customer. Which stage has been reached?
questions.explanation: Operation involves delivering the completed product to the client.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a Waterfall stage?
questions.explanation: The five stages are Requirements, Design, Implementation, Testing, and Operation.

questions.prompt: A team tests the application on several environments and checks different use cases. What are they trying to achieve?
questions.explanation: Testing should cover different use cases and environments to ensure a good user experience.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes Waterfall's flexibility?
choices: It is highly flexible throughout the project
It is relatively inflexible because phases follow a fixed sequence
questions.explanation: The PDF specifically describes Waterfall as not flexible and requiring phases to be completed sequentially.

questions.prompt: A project has a clear goal, fixed requirements, and detailed planning. Which is a likely benefit of using Waterfall?
questions.explanation: Rigorous planning creates a clear structure, while sequential phases make project progress easier to track.
